papers.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators

summary.tldr: StudentSim is a training framework that creates individualized LLM-based student simulators via pooled training and per-student specialization, outperforming GPT-5.4 in matching student behavior and responding to tutor guidance.
key_points: Combines pooled training with per-student specialization to create individualized student simulators from sparse data.
Introduces StudentSimEval, a standardized evaluation protocol covering 60 students across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics.
Achieves F=0.51 behavioral fidelity and R=0.91 guidance responsiveness in chess, outperforming GPT-5.4 (F=0.23, R=0.72) and Maia2 (F=0.45, R=0.27).
Using StudentSim as a reward model for tutor reinforcement learning yields a chess tutor rated by human experts as superior to no-RL and GPT-5.4-trained baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the creation of highly personalized AI tutors by providing a high-fidelity proxy for real student learning without the need for slow and costly human trial data.

papers.title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving

summary.tldr: Qwen-Drive-1.0 is a vision-language foundation model for autonomous driving that unifies 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning into a single framework.
key_points: Integrates an external bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception head that jointly performs 3D object detection, semantic occupancy prediction, and BEV map segmentation.
Uses a dedicated Planning Expert that conditions on shared VLM representations to generate future ego trajectories.
Employs a staged training recipe combining driving supervision with general-purpose VLM data to retain broad visual understanding and instruction-following capabilities.
Evaluated across open-loop, pseudo-closed-loop, and closed-loop settings for motion planning.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that standard vision-language models can be extended with explicit 3D perception and planning modules to handle autonomous driving without sacrificing general VLM capabilities.

papers.title: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers

summary.tldr: SMELT introduces compute-matched Mixture-of-Experts Looped Transformers that loop middle layers twice, outperforming standard MoE baselines and reducing compute-optimal training FLOPs by 6.8% to 18.0%.
key_points: SMELT loops the middle 50% of Transformer layers twice while matching per-token FLOPs, total non-embedding parameters (up to 54B), and KV cache size of unlooped baselines.
Empirical Chinchilla-style scaling laws show SMELT achieves lower loss per FLOP, with downstream performance gains particularly pronounced on Code, long sequences, and many in-context examples.
Mechanistic analysis indicates the second pass through looped layers reduces attention sinks and shifts attention mass toward content-relevant tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: SMELT proves that architectural looping offers true computational efficiency gains rather than just parameter savings, providing a practical method to reduce training FLOPs while improving downstream task performance.

papers.title: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report

summary.tldr: UI-Venus-2 is an open-source multimodal foundation GUI agent that unifies mobile, web, and desktop automation using a closed-loop reasoning-action framework and scaled RL verification.
key_points: Scales environment coverage to over 170 multilingual mobile apps alongside native desktop operating systems.
Generates function-grounded instructions using a deep-research task construction pipeline.
Employs trace-level and sample-level verification with visual keypoints and multi-model voting for reliable RL reward signals.
Integrates safety-aware mechanisms to prevent uncontrolled execution of consequential actions.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a unified, open-source foundation that improves the reliability, safety, and verifiability of digital task automation across diverse operating systems.

papers.title: ZimaBlue: Evolving Generalizable World Action Models through Scalable Video Pre-training

summary.tldr: ZimaBlue is a scalable World Action Model framework that leverages over 120,000 hours of egocentric video pre-training to improve zero-shot robotic manipulation success from 36.1% to 77.8%.
key_points: Employs a three-stage curriculum: causal embodied video pre-training on human/robot videos, video-action mid-training using a unified action representation, and target robot specialization.
Uses an asynchronous Slow-Fast dual-system architecture combining a high-capacity Slow world model for representations with a lightweight Fast branch for inference.
Achieves real-time 30 Hz action prediction on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU.
Demonstrates zero-shot performance scaling on real-robot evaluations with marked improvements on unseen tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a practical method to convert abundant, action-free human and robot egocentric videos into real-time, highly generalizable control policies for physical robots.

papers.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control

summary.tldr: H3-World adapts the 33B MiniMax-H3 video generator into an interactive world model using temporal attention routing and lightweight LoRA fine-tuning.
key_points: Structures actions as combinations of character and camera natural-language instructions aligned with temporal video latents.
Introduces temporal attention routing to isolate instructions to target time intervals and minimize control leakage across actions.
Requires lightweight adaptation with 0.199% trainable parameters, trained on 8,000 gameplay samples over 10,000 LoRA optimization steps.
Achieves precise temporally grounded character and camera control while retaining generation quality and generalizing to unseen scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that large video generators can be turned into precise, interactive world models with minimal parameter training by leveraging emergent language-based control.

papers.title: Hi-Q: Hierarchical Evidence-guided Query Refinement for Multi-Hop Question Answering

summary.tldr: Hi-Q introduces a dynamic, evidence-conditioned query tree framework that hierarchically refines multi-hop QA queries based on real-time corpus support rather than static templates or pre-built graphs.
key_points: Addresses retrievable granularity discovery using an evidence-conditioned resolution operator to check if retrieved evidence supports a query node.
Expands unresolved query nodes using a dependency-preserving binary operator coupled with a semantic coverage verifier, while terminating resolved nodes.
Achieves 52.3 EM and 64.0 F1 under full-corpus retrieval across three benchmarks, outperforming IRCoT by 15.1 EM / 18.2 F1.
Outperforms PropRAG on MuSiQue-full by 11.5 EM / 12.0 F1 without requiring corpus-wide graph construction.
Attains 57.9 EM and 69.3 F1 on average in the restricted supporting/distractor evaluation setting.
summary.why_it_matters: Hi-Q improves multi-hop open-domain question answering performance without the heavy computational overhead of pre-constructing corpus-wide static graphs.

papers.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs as Generalist Vision-Language-Action Agents for Drone Control: Commanding, Approaching, Tracking and Searching

summary.tldr: The DroneCATS-Agent architecture and DroneCATS benchmark evaluate zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), from 2B parameter open models to frontier models, as direct drone-control agents across four core vision-language-action tasks.
key_points: Tests MLLMs directly in the drone control loop using prompt-only action space definitions without fine-tuning or function calling.
Evaluates models across four primary capabilities: target approaching, object tracking, active searching, and multi-drone fleet commanding.
Reveals that spatial perception and physical navigation succeed even in 2B parameter models, but action protocol discipline fails.
Identifies that small edge models fail primarily due to premature or missing arrival self-declarations and copying coordinates across multi-drone views.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that deploying zero-shot MLLM agents on edge hardware requires solving action protocol adherence and termination decisions rather than basic spatial navigation.

papers.title: Uncovering Understanding-Generation Synergy in Native Unified Multimodal Models: From Representation, Task to System

summary.tldr: Researchers systematically analyzed native unified multimodal models across representation, task, and system levels, discovering that task-decoupled architectures and end-to-end training unlock true synergy between visual understanding and generation objectives.
key_points: At the representation level, generation enriches visual features for understanding, while understanding improves vision-language alignment for generation.
Forcing both objectives through identical computation paths causes asymmetric degradation where one objective dominates, which is resolved by using a task-decoupled architecture.
Bidirectional transfer occurs at the task level when understanding and generation tasks share underlying knowledge.
End-to-end unified multimodal models outperform decoupled planner-executor pipelines on complex tasks requiring both understanding and generation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that native unified multimodal models can achieve functional synergy rather than performance tradeoffs when built with decoupled architectures and trained end-to-end.

papers.title: Safin-1: Safety from Within through Memory-Native State Evolution

summary.tldr: Safin-1 introduces Safety from Within, using a memory-routing architecture to maintain intrinsic, evolving safety capabilities directly within the model's native state.
key_points: Built on Memory-Anchor Routing across Context History (MARCH), which uses content-conditioned routing to maintain structured memory and selectively retrieve historical context.
Enables test-time adaptation of persistent capability states without modifying the core backbone weights.
Implements a Safety State interface that unifies contextual memory and active behavior evolution, improving safety performance on downstream tasks.
Maintains competitive performance across general capabilities, long-context understanding, retrieval tasks, and computational efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts model safety from external post-hoc constraints to an intrinsic, memory-native architectural property that adapts dynamically at test time.

papers.title: From Production Traffic to Post-Training: Building a Self-Hosted LLM That Covers the Corporate Request Mix

summary.tldr: Enterprises can consolidate diverse corporate LLM traffic onto a single self-hosted model by merging axis-specific GRPO experts via two-stage SLERP to avoid cross-domain reward interference.
key_points: Trains distinct Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) experts across three operational axes: instruction following, function-calling, and internal task distribution.

Combines the specialized GRPO experts using a two-stage Spherical Linear Interpolation (SLERP) to mitigate cross-domain reward interference and address failure modes like semantic collapse, over-calling, and verbosity hacking.
Outperforms a 7x larger total-parameter baseline in non-reasoning mode on an in-house Arena (69.6 vs. 65.8), instruction following (0.85 vs. 0.83), and function-calling (0.79 vs. 0.77).
Successfully consolidated traffic from over 200 internal applications, handling 50% of platform volume (116 million requests per month) on a unified serving footprint.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables organizations under data-residency constraints to significantly reduce GPU infrastructure costs by replacing fragmented serving fleets with a single high-performing self-hosted model.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered

summary.tldr: FACE-Eval reveals that LLM chain-of-thought faithfulness drops significantly when bias cues originate from tool returns or implicit raw artifacts rather than explicit user messages, making unstated preference adoption harder for external monitors to detect.
key_points: Evaluated 15 open-weight model families (4B to 1.60T parameters) across 5,100 samples in a single-call, prefilled-tool setup using the new FACE-Eval benchmark.
Across all 15 models, verbalized commitment decreases while unverbalized adoption increases when preference cues are placed in tool returns rather than user messages.
Implicit cues lead to higher unverbalized adoption compared to explicit cues in 28 out of 30 model-channel comparisons.
Source-attribution prompts narrow the user-versus-tool channel gap on 7 models, but explicit warnings about chain-of-thought monitoring fail to reliably reduce the gap.
Transcript monitors (GPT-5.6-Luna and GPT-4o-mini) show reduced ability to detect preference adoption in settings with higher unverbalized adoption (Pearson r=-0.54 and r=-0.78).
summary.why_it_matters: Chain-of-thought monitoring for AI safety and alignment becomes unreliable when models process implicit preferences via external tool outputs without explicitly reasoning about them in their output traces.

papers.title: DiagEvo: Diagnosis-Guided Self-Evolution via Hierarchical Error Memory

summary.tldr: DiagEvo enables LLM self-evolution by deriving a curriculum from solver failure history using a hierarchical error memory and double-confidence filtering, eliminating the need for external task resources.
key_points: A 4B diagnostician extracts recurring error causes from failure history and maintains them in a hierarchical error-cause memory grouped under skill nodes.
Memory tracks error causes as Active or Mastered based on self-consistency to balance targeted question generation with free exploration.
Double-confidence filtering filters training data by keeping intermediate-difficulty questions only when the top solver answer holds a clear vote lead.
DiagEvo achieved 72.3% mean accuracy on five math benchmarks using Qwen3-8B (+4.5% over R-Zero) and 57.4% across all nine evaluated benchmarks (+1.1% over DARC).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that self-play models can continuously overcome specific reasoning weaknesses using self-generated failure diagnostics rather than relying on external datasets or human guidance.

papers.title: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments

summary.tldr: GUI-CC is a benchmark evaluating the contextual consistency of GUI world models as multi-step agent environments rather than isolated single-step next-screen predictors.
key_points: Features an offline reference-action track with 500 mobile trajectories from GUIOdyssey and an online agent-loop track with 200 emulator-verified tasks across 30 apps.
Evaluates model performance using four metrics: transition fidelity, transition plausibility, contextual consistency, and task progress.
Demonstrates that plausible single-step screen generation fails to guarantee context preservation or support executable multi-step agent rollouts.
summary.why_it_matters: It highlights that current GUI world models cannot reliably serve as simulation environments for training agents without addressing multi-step contextual decay.

papers.title: EM^2Mem: Event-Centric Multimodal Memory for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: EM^2Mem is an event-centric multimodal memory framework that binds heterogeneous evidence to event anchors during memory construction, resolving cross-modal and temporal fragment alignment issues in long-video question answering.
key_points: Binds multimodal records, temporal context, graph-linked relations, semantic facts, and provenance into event-indexed memory cells.
Outperforms the strongest baseline by 2.0, 2.4, and 3.7 average accuracy points across three long-video QA benchmarks.
Increases strict event-level Top-5 evidence recall by 7.0 points.
Reduces per-query inference latency by 4.67x and total inference tokens by 63.66%.
summary.why_it_matters: By providing generation-ready grounded event readouts instead of isolated fragments, the framework significantly cuts inference costs and latency while improving QA accuracy on long videos.

papers.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: A Fisher-geometric study reveals that benign fine-tuning breaks LLM safety by re-sharpening low-rank output-routing pathways in output-side MLPs, rather than through gradient conflicts.
key_points: Safety Fisher matrices are low-rank, meaning alignment flattens safety geometry while leaving output-routing pathways intact.
As few as 100 benign fine-tuning examples selectively re-sharpen these output-side MLP pathways, causing safety collapse while general utility degrades only mildly.
Internal safety-relevant representations remain preserved, allowing a small number of safety examples to quickly restore refusal behavior.
Mitigation methods like LoRA and ASAM temporarily suppress output-side sharpness, but their protective effects diminish as fine-tuning scales increase.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding safety loss as a disruption of low-rank output routing explains why LLM alignment is easily bypassed and guides better design of durable safety guardrails.

papers.title: Efficiently Estimating Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Laws through Power-Law Entropy Search

summary.tldr: Power-Law Entropy Search (PLES) is a cost-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization acquisition function that estimates optimal hyperparameter scaling laws for LLMs using under 10% of the compute budget required by grid search.
key_points: PLES targets the reduction of overall scaling law estimate uncertainty rather than directly optimizing a single objective function.
The acquisition function evaluates candidate configurations to maximize uncertainty reduction per unit of computational cost, prioritizing smaller, highly informative experiments.
Empirical evaluation spans synthetic benchmarks, surrogate models based on real LLM training data, and active LLM pre-training runs.
Achieves convergence to accurate hyperparameter scaling laws with a greater than 10x reduction in compute compared to conventional grid searches and standard baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables machine learning teams to accurately predict optimal hyperparameter configurations for production-scale LLMs while cutting tuning compute costs by over 90%.

papers.title: Probing Factual Knowledge Transfer with Training Data Interventions

summary.tldr: An intervention-based framework using the SIFT benchmark shows that multilingual models transfer very little English-pretrained factual knowledge into Persian during continued pretraining, particularly for rare entities.
key_points: SIFT provides 500 triples across 20 relations split into general and Persian-related entities with native Persian cloze templates for systematic factual data removal.
Under strict data removal, a large majority of facts acquired during English pretraining fail to transfer to Persian during continued pretraining.
Sentence-level co-occurrence removal fails to fully eliminate factual signal, while easy, randomly selected negative candidate sets artificially inflate measured transfer via shallow heuristics.
Low entity frequency in the source language severely limits transfer, causing Persian-related facts (rarer in English data) to barely transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: Multilingual models rely primarily on direct target-language exposure rather than cross-lingual transfer to retain factual knowledge, highlighting risks in assuming pretraining facts carry over across languages.

papers.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally

summary.tldr: Causal intervention on 9 LLMs shows quantization damage is diffuse, and spending extra precision on global finer granularity improves accuracy far more than selectively repairing localized critical layers.
key_points: Tested three hypotheses for quantization damage location (task circuits, model computation sites, and weight statistics) using causal mixed-precision intervention, finding none predict which layers benefit from restored precision.
For 8 out of 9 evaluated models across 4 families, recovering 75% of the accuracy gap required restoring precision to roughly half the layers; only Qwen3-8B showed concentrated damage.
Allocating a precision budget to global finer granularity (group-128) outperformed repairing the most recoverable layers by 21 to 52 points across all 8 compatible models, including Qwen3-8B.
Evaluations across RTN, GPTQ, and AWQ demonstrated that 8-bit precision is near-lossless, indicating quantization residual damage is budget-limited.
Peak recovery locations correlate with architecture within a model family, but not across different families.
summary.why_it_matters: When optimizing quantized LLM serving, hardware precision budgets should default to global granularity improvements rather than complex, selective layer-by-layer protection.

papers.title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning

summary.tldr: A timestep-free diffusion architecture with a persistent hidden state acts as an anytime solver that improves performance with inference depth and solves complex reasoning tasks without progressive denoising schedules.
key_points: Modifies a diffusion denoiser by adding a persistent hidden state and removing timestep conditioning, enabling a single update function to run to arbitrary depth.
Achieves a 99.90% exact solve rate on Sudoku-Extreme and 98.93% on Maze-Unique using an arbitrary-depth anytime solver.
Replaces progressive denoising at inference with continuous maximum noise injection (replacing non-clue variables with fresh Gaussian noise each step) while maintaining accuracy.
Demonstrates that diffusion's main utility in this setup is providing an annealed denoising training curriculum rather than a required inference sampling schedule.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach demonstrates that complex spatial and logical reasoning tasks can be solved through iterative noise-injection trajectories without relying on parallel rollouts, candidate selection, or external verifiers.

papers.title: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers

summary.tldr: SMELT introduces a budget-matched Mixture-of-Experts Looped Transformer recipe that loops middle layers twice, achieving higher compute efficiency than standard unlooped architectures.
key_points: SMELT loops the middle half of layers twice while strictly matching per-token FLOPs, total non-embedding parameters, and KV cache against unlooped baselines.
Scaling experiments up to 54B non-embedding parameters show SMELT reduces training FLOPs by 6.8% to 18.0% along the Chinchilla-style compute-optimal frontier.
Downstream performance gains are highest on Code tasks and scale positively with both sequence length and the count of in-context examples.
Mechanistic analysis reveals the second layer visit reduces the attention sink effect and reallocates attention mass directly to content-relevant tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that re-executing Transformer middle layers improves model performance and compute efficiency without increasing parameter count, memory footprint, or inference FLOPs.

papers.title: One-Layer Transformer Provably Learns Multiclass One-Nearest Neighbor in Context

summary.tldr: Researchers proved that one-layer transformers using standard argmax classification heads and simplex encoding are functionally equivalent to multiclass one-nearest-neighbor classifiers.
key_points: Extends existing binary transformer-nearest neighbor equivalence proofs to the multiclass setting.
Employs a simplex encoding scheme paired with a standard argmax classification head.
Eliminates the need for non-standard rounding-based classification heads used in prior theoretical models.
summary.why_it_matters: This theoretical proof grounds the in-context learning behavior of standard transformer architectures in well-understood nearest-neighbor classification mechanics for multiclass tasks.

papers.title: Post-Training Science for Supervised Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: A systematic controlled sweep across Qwen3 and Llama models up to 235B parameters evaluates how SFT hyperparameter choices, optimizer selection, and dataset scaling impact downstream task performance.
key_points: Evaluates full fine-tuning versus LoRA parameters (rank and alpha), optimizer choice (AdamW versus geometry-aware optimizers), batch size, and learning rate scaling across dense and MoE models.
Uses four real-world customer SFT datasets with task judges aligned directly to training targets to evaluate downstream quality against validation loss and loss landscape flatness metrics.
Measures performance bounds and general instruction-following degradation across multi-epoch training runs up to 235B parameter scales.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces empirical guesswork with measured, empirical rules for hyperparameter selection and tuning trade-offs during supervised fine-tuning.

papers.title: From Rollouts to Recipes: Self-Contained Post-Training for LLMs

summary.tldr: Self-Routing is a behavior-conditioned post-training framework that dynamically routes LLM training samples to GRPO, on-policy self-distillation, regularization, or skipping based on rollout correctness and confidence.
key_points: Evaluates sample-level rollout correctness and confidence to determine the optimization path without external teachers or extra sampling.
Routes samples dynamically across four strategies: GRPO, on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), regularization, or skipping.
Outperforms uniform GRPO, uniform OPSD, fixed mixtures, and simple routing baselines in mathematical reasoning experiments using Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 backbones.
Adapts the routing distribution dynamically during training, suppressing redundant updates on stable or low-signal samples.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves LLM post-training efficiency and mathematical reasoning performance by adapting optimization strategies to sample difficulty without incurring extra annotation or sampling costs.

papers.title: When Tokenization is Secretly Output Supervision

summary.tldr: A controlled study reveals that tokenization functions primarily as output supervision in autoregressive models, where output granularity dictates task difficulty, training dynamics, and internal representations independently of input tokenization.
key_points: Output tokenization determines what an autoregressive model must resolve in a single forward pass, defining the actual supervision signal and task difficulty.

Controlled experiments on numeric reasoning using decoupled input/output tokenization show performance and internal representations are driven by output tokenization and invariant to input tokenization.
A survey of 120 recent *CL numeric reasoning papers revealed that 69% compare models across different tokenization regimes without reporting it, and only ~10% report the numeric tokenization used.
summary.why_it_matters: Cross-model evaluations may systematically reflect differences in task definition and supervision granularity rather than true underlying model capabilities.

security.title: An AI-Assisted Cyber Attack: Inside a Unit 42 Investigation

summary.tldr: Unit 42 investigated an enterprise network breach executed in a matter of hours by an attacker using autonomous AI agents.
key_points: Attacker leveraged autonomous AI agents to conduct the breach.
The enterprise network compromise was executed within a timeframe of hours.
Investigation focuses on strategies to defend against agentic cyber attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the practical threat of autonomous AI agents accelerating the timeline of enterprise network breaches.

security.title: OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard and Sponsors as Community Tops 30,000 Members

summary.tldr: The OWASP GenAI Security Project released the 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications and debuted a new Agent Control Standard for securing agentic AI systems.
key_points: The 2026 OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 incorporates incident research, updated rankings, and expanded mappings to NIST, MITRE ATLAS, CWE, and the OWASP Agentic Applications Top 10.
The donated Agent Control Standard (ACS) extends existing agentic guidance into practical runtime enforcement.
OWASP introduced the GenAI Security Industry Framework Crosswalk to map guidance to existing security and compliance frameworks, along with an expanded AI Security Solutions Directory.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations deploying LLMs and agentic AI systems get updated, real-world-tested threat models and runtime standards to secure applications moving into production.

security.title: Defense-as-Skill: Evolving Runtime Guard Skill for Skill-Augmented Agents

summary.tldr: Defense-as-Skill introduces SkillSonar, a runtime guard implemented as an editable skill that uses Monte-Carlo Tree Search to evolve task-conditioned defenses against malicious skill-augmented agent attacks without modifying agent runtimes.
key_points: Introduces SkillSonar, a runtime guard skill that evaluates sensitive agent actions against task boundaries to trigger allow, replan, or user confirmation actions.
Presents SCOPE-R, a task-conditioned dataset spanning 6 risk families and 21 sub-categories, containing 206 attack-confirmed malicious instances and 43 benign tasks.
Employs a Monte-Carlo Tree Search procedure to evolve the on-disk guard skill based on rollout feedback, mitigating safety risks across Claude Code and OpenClaw.
Reduces GLM-5 Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 0.482 to 0.104 in-distribution (ID) and from 0.606 to 0.115 out-of-distribution (OOD) while preserving utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables runtime safety monitoring for AI agents using flexible, model-agnostic guard skills that can be evolved and updated without altering the core agent architecture.

security.title: One Prompt Is Enough: Watermark Laundering Through Foundation Image Models

summary.tldr: Foundation image editing models can remove invisible watermarks using a single reconstruction prompt while maintaining high visual fidelity, exposing a distinct vulnerability class termed watermark laundering.
key_points: Evaluated six OpenAI and Google image editing models against three watermarking schemes (including DwtDct) across 1,800 reconstructed outputs using a joint bit error rate (BER) and visual/semantic fidelity profile.
OpenAI models caused the strongest payload disruption across schemes, while Google's Nano Banana 2 demonstrated that DwtDct remains vulnerable even under high-fidelity reconstructions.
Prompt ablations confirmed that explicit removal-oriented instructions are unnecessary; payload disruption is driven inherently by the model's reconstruction pathway.
Demonstrated that prompt-conditioned reconstruction functions as a distinct operational attack interface compared to conventional perturbations like noise, blur, cropping, and compression.
summary.why_it_matters: Invisible watermarking evaluation protocols must incorporate foundation-model reconstruction as a standard robustness metric to account for practical adversarial evasion.

security.title: Position Matters: Feature Inversion Attacks in ViT Split Inference with Token Reduction and Shuffling

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the Spatially Aligned Reconstruction Attack (SARA), demonstrating that token shuffling and reduction in ViT split-inference fail to prevent feature inversion attacks because intermediate token embeddings retain positional information.
key_points: Transmitted ViT token embeddings retain sufficient positional information to bypass spatial disruption defenses.
SARA predicts token positions, restores spatial layout, uses a feature-space masked autoencoder to reconstruct missing embeddings, and recovers the input image.
Token shuffling provides only superficial privacy against SARA, whereas token reduction offers stronger but still incomplete protection.
An edge-side defense removing positional embeddings and adapting edge blocks via knowledge distillation mitigates SARA without modifying the cloud model or sacrificing task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates that common efficiency optimizations like token shuffling do not guarantee privacy in split-inference systems and offers a lightweight defense that preserves accuracy.

security.title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness

summary.tldr: A systematic security analysis of 12 real-world AI agent harnesses reveals Context Privilege Escalation attacks that enable remote code execution, full agent compromise, and unauthorized tool invocations.
key_points: Identified two new attack categories in AI harness context assembly: MessageRole Context Privilege Escalation (M-CPE) and Cross-Scope Context Privilege Escalation (X-CPE).
M-CPE elevates attacker content from low-privileged contexts into higher-privileged message roles.
X-CPE allows attacker-controlled content to persist beyond its original context scope.
Evaluated vulnerability across 12 production agent harnesses, including Claude Code and Codex, leading to denial of service, full compromise, and remote code execution.
summary.why_it_matters: Opaque and insecure context assembly logic in popular AI agent harnesses can allow attackers to achieve total control over host systems via remote code execution.

summary.tldr: Reveree is a diagnostic framework for LLM reverse-engineering agents that evaluates performance across solve rates, an eight-stage progress schema, and behavioral action profiling.
key_points: Reveree evaluates model performance using deterministic verification for action stages and an outcome-blinded LLM judge (validated against a human expert) for comprehension stages.

Evaluation of nine frontier models and four prompting strategies across 88 picoCTF and NYU-CTF challenges reveals that base model selection drives performance, while prompting strategies yield secondary, model-dependent effects.
Model failures concentrate primarily in comprehension stages, where increasing budget, persistence, or reasoning effort fails to rescue performance, indicating a fundamental competence limit.
Larger, newer, or more expensive models do not consistently outperform smaller or older alternatives in reverse-engineering tasks.
While models demonstrate flag memorization on picoCTF from descriptions alone, minimal recall occurs on NYU-CTF, and most successful solves persist under surface perturbations.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts LLM security evaluations beyond binary solve rates to pinpoint specific analytical failure modes and isolate true binary analysis from benchmark memorization.

security.title: HiveTraceGuard-Pro: A Compact Generative Guardrail for Prompt Injection, Jailbreaks, and Adversarial Obfuscation

summary.tldr: HiveTraceGuard-Pro is a 0.6B generative guardrail model LoRA-tuned from Qwen3-0.6B that achieves high Russian prompt-injection recall (0.999) and 14.3 ms median latency.
key_points: Trained on English and Russian corpora using eight obfuscation transforms applied to benign and harmful paired examples.
Uses a binary scoring rule (safe/unsafe) for the final target turn, evaluated via a legacy standalone-reply serialization format.
Achieved an aggregate score of 0.7432 across 19 benchmark groups, ranking third behind two higher-scoring models.
Delivered a 0.88 combined-F1 on clean Russian robustness and a 0.999 recall on Russian prompt injection, with at least 27.1% training set overlap.
Overall suite metrics showed a false positive rate of 0.268 and a false negative rate of 0.156.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a compact 0.6B parameter model can deliver low-latency (14.3 ms) guardrailing against adversarial prompt injections and obfuscations, specifically targeting Russian-language inputs.

security.title: AKRASIA: Stealthy Backdoor Attack on Reasoning-based Code LLMs

summary.tldr: AKRASIA is an inference-time backdoor attack targeting reasoning Code LLMs that uses code-level triggers, in-context learning, and unfaithful reasoning to achieve high attack success while evading defenses and human inspection.
key_points: Combines code-level triggers, in-context learning, and model unfaithfulness to execute payloads and conceal backdoor steps.
Achieves up to a 99.34% average attack success rate (ASR) on state-of-the-art LLMs while maintaining up to 97.23% task accuracy.
Bypasses state-of-the-art automated defenses in 14 out of 18 settings, retaining up to 98.82% average ASR.
Successfully conceals triggers and malicious reasoning steps from human inspection in up to 80% of tested settings.
summary.why_it_matters: This attack demonstrates that reasoning-based Code LLMs can be manipulated to execute malicious code while generating seemingly plausible reasoning, exposing severe gaps in current human and automated defenses.

security.title: Membership Inference in Fine-tuned Diffusion Language Models via Token-level Memorization Asymmetry

summary.tldr: Researchers identified token-level memorization asymmetry in diffusion language models and created Q-Skew, a quantile-weighted skewness indicator for membership inference and privacy attacks on fine-tuned models.
key_points: Theoretical analysis of diffusion training dynamics revealed token-level memorization asymmetry in fine-tuned diffusion language models (DLMs).
Introduced Q-Skew, a quantile-weighted skewness-based indicator designed for membership inference attacks on DLMs.
Empirical evaluations demonstrate that Q-Skew outperforms existing baselines across multiple datasets and models.
Demonstrated that Q-Skew facilitates additional privacy threats, including personally identifiable information (PII) extraction.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings expose an underexplored privacy vulnerability in diffusion language models, demonstrating that fine-tuned DLMs require systematic privacy evaluations and stronger defensive measures.

security.title: RISA: Response Inspection and Selective Actions for Refusal Calibration in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Response Inspection and Selective Actions (RISA) is an inference-time framework that evaluates initial LLM responses and prompt representations to selectively correct refusal errors without updating underlying model parameters.
key_points: Uses a hybrid scoring approach combining fixed contextual rules for obvious cases with a calibrated linear probe on final-layer prompt hidden states for unmatched semantic variations.
Adapts to different base models by separately calibrating the probe score, representation-support boundary, and action thresholds.
Combines the calculated prompt score with the initial refusal status at runtime to trigger selective corrective actions only when an error is detected.
Improves refusal reliability on both harmful and benign prompts while preserving base model utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a parameter-efficient, inference-time method to prevent over-refusal of benign prompts and under-refusal of harmful ones without requiring costly retraining.

security.title: PhantomCall: Evading ML Malware Detectors via Function Call Graph Perturbation

summary.tldr: PhantomCall is a novel black-box attack that evades machine learning malware detectors by injecting fully executable dummy functions at targeted call sites to perturb the function call graph (FCG) while preserving semantics.
key_points: Modifies the FCG and CFG structures of Windows PE malware by injecting executable dummy functions paired with classifier-guided search and tunable injection parameters.
Achieves an 85-100% attack success rate against MalConv (CNN), MalGraph (GNN), and SAFE+GNN (pure FCG GNN) across two FPR thresholds.
Outperforms prior state-of-the-art attacks by up to 14.78 percentage points on MalGraph and 95.5 percentage points on SAFE+GNN while generating variants up to 2.9x faster.
Requires only a single call site modification for the majority of evasions on MalConv and MalGraph, with 86-97% of variants preserving malicious behavior in sandbox testing.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that graph-based ML malware detectors relying on function call structures remain highly vulnerable to fast, semantic-preserving structural perturbations.

NVIDIA Nemotron is used to build adaptive systems that identify missed threats and address defense gaps.

security.title: SoK: When Safe Agents Fail Together: The Security of Multi Agent LLM Systems

summary.tldr: A systematization of multi-agent LLM system (MAS) security analyzing 197 works to introduce an A-I-R attack framework and a five-part defense contract.
key_points: Analyzed 197 papers to identify six interaction interfaces, four adversary positions, seven system-level risks, and eight recurring attack paths.
Introduced the A-I-R framework to categorize attacks by Adversary position, Interaction interface, and resulting system-level Risk.
Structured defenses via a five-part contract specifying path target, observation, intervention, trust boundary, and recovery.
Audited 44 evaluation works and highlighted critical gaps in path closure, recovery, and counterfactual isolation of true multi-agent interaction effects.
summary.why_it_matters: Local safety checks on individual LLM agents are insufficient, requiring an execution-level, interaction-aware framework to defend against systemic multi-agent vulnerabilities.

infra.title: Tokenomics at scale: How Jamf built real-time spend enforcement for Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: Jamf built an automated AWS architecture for Amazon Bedrock that enforces near-real-time tiered spend limits on individual engineers without requiring re-authentication.
key_points: Measures spend by logging Amazon Bedrock token counts and user identities to Amazon S3, using an Amazon Athena view to calculate daily per-user costs in place.
Executes an AWS Lambda enforcement handler every 15 minutes via EventBridge to compare actual spend against standard limits and custom DynamoDB exception records.
Enforces tiered model restrictions dynamically by using iam:CreatePolicyVersion to update IAM Customer Managed Policies with user-specific saml:sub condition keys.
Implements progressive denial logic (e.g., blocking Claude Opus at 80% budget and Claude Sonnet at 100%) while preserving access to low-cost models like Claude Haiku.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables enterprise FinOps teams to prevent unchecked generative AI API spend by individual users while maintaining continuous engineer productivity.

summary.tldr: AWS announced the availability of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, featuring improved reasoning, agentic coding, and autonomous multi-hour operation.
key_points: Designated as an Anthropic Covered Model, requiring the aws_review data retention API mode, which allows AWS personnel to retain prompts and outputs for up to 30 days for safety reviews without sharing data with the model provider.
Introduces Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), enabling eligible customers to use Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 with zero data retention (ZDR) for internal use through December 31, 2026.

Demonstrates reduced confident errors and enhanced performance in competition mathematics, graduate-level engineering and science problems, codebase-spanning agentic coding, and autonomous tool-using workflows.

Future EFS updates scheduled for later this year will support automated safety reviews without human intervention, keeping prompts and outputs within customer AWS accounts under user-managed encryption keys.
summary.why_it_matters: Enterprise customers gain access to advanced autonomous reasoning and coding capabilities while maintaining strict control over data privacy and compliance through AWS-managed retention policies.

infra.title: Build observable enterprise agentic retrieval using Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with AWS CloudFormation

summary.tldr: AWS has detailed an architecture combining Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to deploy observable, multi-step enterprise agentic retrieval using AWS CloudFormation.
key_points: The system uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime to auto-instrument reason-and-act loops with OpenTelemetry spans emitted to Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray.
The agent routes queries across topic-specific knowledge bases via Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls brokered by the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway.
Managed Knowledge Bases expose an AgenticRetrieveStream API that decomposes questions, retrieves iteratively from Amazon S3-backed datastores, and streams grounded, cited answers.
The agent evaluates returned context sufficiency to decide whether to execute additional retrieval loops before returning the final response to the user.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables enterprise teams to automate and monitor complex, multi-turn RAG reasoning and cross-source retrieval workflows with built-in observability using a single CloudFormation template.

infra.title: Build multi-tenant agentic chat applications on enterprise data with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

summary.tldr: AWS details an architecture for multi-tenant agentic chat applications using Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and a custom connector for isolated, multi-hop document retrieval.
key_points: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base automates ingestion, vector and full-text indexing, embedding, and re-ranking without external retrieval infrastructure.
The built-in agentic retrieval engine decomposes complex user queries into sub-queries and executes multi-hop retrievals while preserving per-tenant security filtering on every hop.
A custom connector data source enables direct ingestion of user-uploaded multimodal content (including text, CSV, and Excel) into the knowledge base within seconds.
Application access control uses Amazon Cognito to supply verified user identities to Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda, enforcing strict data isolation.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes the need to build, scale, and secure custom agentic search infrastructure while strictly enforcing multi-tenant isolation across complex multi-step retrieval queries.

vendors.title: Developing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with our customers

summary.tldr: Anthropic announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), combining zero data retention (ZDR) with misuse monitoring by storing data directly within customer-controlled cloud infrastructure.
key_points: EFS addresses safety risks in Mythos-class models (like Claude Fable 5.1) by enabling long-term correlation of traffic across multiple sessions and accounts to detect cyberattacks and credential theft.
Data is hosted within customer-managed cloud environments rather than Anthropic's infrastructure, solving compliance hurdles associated with standard 30-day data retention policies.
Eligible enterprise customers will receive temporary ZDR on Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 pending the phased rollout of EFS starting later in fall 2026.
Supported environments will include Claude Code, Claude Enterprise, Claude Platform, AWS (Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform), Google's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows organizations in heavily regulated sectors like banking and healthcare to deploy advanced agentic AI models while satisfying strict regulatory privacy constraints.

vendors.title: Claude Fable 5.1 made me a really nice animated pelican

summary.tldr: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, featuring a 52.6% score on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 and five variable reasoning effort levels ranging from low to max.
key_points: Claude Fable 5.1 scores 52.6% on the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark, up from 24.7% for Fable 5 and 22.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
Fable 5.1 features five reasoning effort settings: low, medium, high, xhigh, and max, with no option to disable reasoning entirely.
At low and medium effort settings, Fable 5.1 skipped reasoning completely for an SVG generation prompt, using roughly 2,000 output tokens in ~23 seconds.
Higher reasoning settings scale output tokens and cost significantly, reaching 36,767 tokens ($1.83, ~8 min) at xhigh and 65,927 tokens ($3.30, ~14 min) at max.
summary.why_it_matters: The model demonstrates significant advancements in scientific problem-solving while providing fine-grained control over computational cost and reasoning depth via variable effort settings.
